questions.stem: Which is the most common benign tumor of the liver?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hemangioma
  • Hepatic Hemangioma aka Cavernous hemangiomas, is the most common benign tumor of the liver.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 669,667

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding hepatoblastoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: It is a type of small round-cell tumor

options.label: B
options.text: It is the most common liver tumor in early childhood

options.label: C
options.text: FOX p3 gene mutation is most commonly seen

options.label: D
options.text: It may be associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome

questions.answerText: FOX p3 gene mutation is most commonly seen
questions.solutionHtml:
FOX p3 gene mutation is most commonly seen
  • The genetic mutations commonly seen in hepatoblastoma involve the Wnt signaling pathway, such as CTNNB1 and WTX mutations, not FOX p3 gene mutation.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 669

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding hepatocellular carcinoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is a risk factor

options.label: D
options.text: Metastasis occurs via direct invasion, hematogenous or lymphatic route

questions.solutionHtml:
Serum AFP levels are normal
  • Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels are often elevated in patients with HCC, and AFP can be used as a diagnostic and prognostic marker for HCC.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 669,670

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old patient, a chronic alcoholic presented with a history of weight loss, and jaundice. A liver biopsy is done and the image is shown below. Based on histological features, what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hepatocellular carcinoma
  • The given clinical scenario and a histopathological image showing nests of hepatocytes with nuclear atypia are suggestive of Hepatocellular carcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 669,670

questions.stemHtml: A 65-year-old patient, who is a chronic alcoholic presented with a history of weight loss, jaundice and massive ascites, and further deteriorating condition. A liver biopsy is shown below based on histological features what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cirrhosis
  • The given clinical history of chronic alcoholism and histological features of fibrosis suggests the diagnosis of Cirrhosis.
  • Cirrhosis is characterized by the development of fibrosis and the disruption of normal liver architecture.
  • Alcoholic  hepatitis  is  often  accompanied  by  prominent  activation  of  sinusoidal  stellate  cells  and portal  fibroblasts,  giving  rise  to  fibrosis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 640,641

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding the fibrolamellar variant of HCC?
questions.solutionHtml:
No association with cirrhosis
  • Fibrolamellar carcinoma is a distinctive  variant  of  HCC which do not have an association with cirrhosis, alcoholism, or hepatitis B/C infection.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 669,670
